title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a law designed to require the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how it uses artificial intelligence in its operations and decision‑making processes. The act aims to increase accountability and trust among veterans by making AI systems and their outcomes publicly available.

title: To establish a human-centered Federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce, promote the ethical and responsible teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, provide for equitable access to artificial intelligence-ready workforce development, safeguard student and worker data privacy, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy proposes a federal, people‑focused framework for bringing artificial intelligence into schools and the workplace, with an emphasis on ethical and responsible teaching. It also seeks to guarantee fair access to AI‑ready job training, protect the privacy of students and workers, and cover other related concerns.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to create a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. The program will be overseen by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and is intended to test new AI tools for detecting, responding to, and mitigating cyber attacks on essential services.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act proposes measures to strengthen the security of advanced artificial intelligence systems, ensuring they are resilient against threats and misuse. It encourages the development of robust safeguards, oversight protocols, and research into AI safety to protect national interests and public safety.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act prohibits using artificial intelligence to automatically deny Medicare claims, requiring that all denials be reviewed and decided by a human. The law also mandates transparency about the decision criteria and protects patients from potentially unfair or inaccurate AI‑based denials.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes to temporarily halt the construction and operation of new AI data centers in order to address environmental, energy, and societal concerns. It aims to give lawmakers time to develop comprehensive regulations for AI infrastructure.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb companies from charging excessive fees for AI services and from using AI to manipulate labor markets. It proposes regulations that mandate transparent pricing and fair wage practices, protecting consumers and workers from exploitative behavior.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is designed to protect U.S. AI models from unauthorized copying or use by foreign parties. It establishes legal penalties, reporting requirements, and enforcement mechanisms to make it harder for stolen models to be sold or deployed abroad.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 creates a formal program to study how artificial intelligence is used in judicial processes and to evaluate its effects on fairness, accuracy, and efficiency. It also sets up oversight bodies and reporting requirements to monitor AI tools in courts, ensuring transparency and accountability for their deployment.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 establishes rules for how the U.S. Small Business Administration will adopt and manage AI technologies in its operations. It sets out safeguards, transparency requirements, and oversight measures to ensure that AI use by the SBA meets federal standards and protects the interests of businesses and consumers.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard shoppers and users from misleading or false claims made by AI‑generated content. It sets rules that require clear disclosure and honest labeling of AI‑driven products and services to prevent deceptive marketing or exploitation.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act is a proposed U.S. law that seeks to position the United States as a global AI leader while ensuring consistent, nationwide standards and regulations for AI technology. It aims to coordinate federal, state, and industry efforts to foster innovation, safety, and equitable benefits of AI across the country.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with AI systems. It requires federal agencies and industry partners to conduct standardized risk evaluations, maintain transparency, and report potential safety concerns to an oversight body to protect public welfare.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act aims to encourage the use of artificial intelligence in banking, lending, and investment services by providing clear regulatory guidance. It seeks to balance rapid innovation with consumer protection by setting standards and safeguards for AI deployment in the financial industry.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act aims to boost AI research capabilities at historically Black colleges and universities. It provides funding, resources, and strategic partnerships to help these institutions become leaders in AI innovation.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law that would require U.S. schools to teach students about artificial intelligence. It aims to give kids the skills and knowledge they need to understand, use, and safely engage with AI technologies in their everyday lives.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to keep people safe from misleading or dishonest artificial‑intelligence systems by setting clear rules for how AI can be used and marketed. The law requires companies to disclose when a product or service uses AI, to explain how it works, and to face penalties if they mislead consumers or hide the AI’s true nature.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act proposes new regulations to guide the responsible development, deployment, and use of artificial‑intelligence models. It focuses on ensuring transparency, accountability, and safety, with the goal of protecting users and society from potential harms associated with advanced AI systems.

title: SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Small Business.
summary: The SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026 requires small businesses to submit regular reports to the Small Business Administration detailing which AI tools they use, how they are applied, and any associated risks or benefits. The law aims to give policymakers a clear picture of AI adoption across the small‑business sector so they can shape regulation, support, and oversight that promotes responsible, transparent, and equitable AI use.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to regulate artificial intelligence development and deployment across the EU, ensuring safety, transparency, and accountability. It introduces a framework for risk assessment, labeling of AI products, and mandatory human oversight for high‑risk applications.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies that use automated decision‑making systems to evaluate their algorithms for bias, fairness, and privacy risks. It would also mandate that firms publicly report these assessments and take corrective action to prevent discriminatory or harmful outcomes.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 is legislation designed to protect individuals from discrimination and bias in AI systems. It establishes standards and enforcement mechanisms to ensure AI technologies uphold civil rights principles such as fairness, transparency, and accountability.

title: To prohibit the manufacture and conveyance of certain products for children that incorporate an artificial intelligence chatbot, and for other purposes.
action: Sponsor introductory remarks on measure. (CR H3000-3001)
summary: This policy bans making or selling child‑targeted products that include an artificial intelligence chatbot. It also addresses other related purposes and safety concerns.

title: To codify Executive Order 14319 (relating to preventing woke AI in the Federal Government).
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The policy aims to put into law Executive Order 14319, which is designed to prevent the use of “woke” AI technologies in the federal government. It establishes rules and guidelines that federal agencies must follow to ensure AI systems remain neutral and free from ideological bias.

title: To amend the Public Health Service Act to update quality standards for mammography facilities for the use of AI systems, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy amends the Public Health Service Act to update quality standards for mammography facilities, specifically addressing the use of AI systems. It also includes other related provisions to ensure safe and effective use of AI in medical imaging.

title: American Leadership in AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committees on Energy and Commerce, Agriculture, Oversight and Government Reform, Education and Workforce, the Judiciary, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American Leadership in AI Act seeks to position the United States at the forefront of artificial intelligence development and deployment. It aims to strengthen national security, boost innovation, and set high standards for responsible AI use across government and industry.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 33 - 0.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2025 establishes federal funding and programs to enhance AI education across K‑12 and higher‑education institutions, aiming to build a skilled workforce ready for an AI‑driven economy. It outlines collaboration between academia, industry, and federal agencies, sets standards for curriculum and assessment, and ensures equitable access to AI learning resources for all students.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act seeks to boost the U.S. AI industry by encouraging the export of all components of AI technology—from hardware and software to data and models—to global markets. It aims to balance commercial growth with national security by establishing guidelines and incentives for companies to comply with export regulations while expanding their reach abroad.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act aims to shield families from the rising costs associated with the energy consumption of AI data centers. It proposes measures to regulate or offset energy expenses so households won’t be burdened by the environmental and economic impacts of AI infrastructure.
